name: graph-command-migration
title: Migrate the proof-or-stop-graph story visualizer into this repo as the proof-or-stop graph command
description:
The interactive story + evidence graph currently lives in a separate untracked repository at ~/work/repo/proof-or-stop-graph (32 commits, no git remote, package @proof-or-stop/graph 0.1.0). It reads Proof-or-Stop story state, builds a node:sqlite FTS5 full-text index, serves a browser client over HTTP, and opens a browser. Its README already designates createApp() and startServer() as the seams a CLI command would call, and src/index.ts is an explicit library surface, so no logic depends on that package's own CLI shell.

This story moves that source into this monorepo as a new packages/graph workspace subpackage and exposes it as the top-level command "proof-or-stop graph", so the visualizer ships with the CLI instead of requiring a separate checkout.

Scope of the code being moved: 9325 lines across src/index.ts, src/core (data.ts, machine.ts, app.ts, store/fn.ts, graph/fn.ts, detail/fn.ts, search/fn.ts, search/worker.ts), src/io (http.ts, open-browser.ts, find-root.ts), src/shells/cli/main.ts, src/shells/web (app.head.html, app.css, app.body.html, graph2d.js, app.js, playback.js, gif-palette.js, gif-encoder.worker.js), src/tasks (audit.ts, bench.ts, anchor-check.mjs), and scripts/build-web.mjs plus scripts/copy-assets.mjs.

Vendored browser bundles (mermaid, d3, gsap, mediabunny, gifenc) are npm dependency build output, not source: they stay gitignored under packages/graph/assets/ and are regenerated by the build, exactly as in the source repo. The same applies to the assembled assets/app.html, which build-web.mjs composes from the src/shells/web parts.

Registering a new top-level command in this repo touches eight fail-closed surfaces, all verified against current code: MAIN_TOOLS in packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts; a COMMAND_POLICIES row in packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts (a missing ownershipClass is rejected fail-closed by the command-ownership-contract task); a handler factory in packages/main/src/handlers/; registerBatch in packages/main/src/registry.ts; the text-only process-fact mirror comment in packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts lines 194-440; DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS in packages/main/src/core/config.ts and READ_ONLY_COMMANDS in packages/main/src/cli/activity-policy.ts; KNOWN_GROUP and KNOWN_ORDER in packages/main/src/cli/help-renderer.ts; and the contract tests command-ownership-contract, command-catalog-smoke, cli-surface-smoke and verify-orphan-surface.

Two cross-cutting facts constrain the work. First, node:sqlite is used nowhere else in this repo and requires Node 22.5 or newer, while no package.json here declares an engines field at all; the graph subpackage therefore needs an explicit engines floor. Second, packages/main ships zero static web assets today (all its dashboard HTML is inline template literals) and has no files field, so the browser client must be served out of packages/graph rather than smuggled through the packages/main tsc output.

Because graph is a long-running server command rather than a request-response handler, it follows the existing dashboard precedent: dashboard is dispatched from a dedicated pre-dispatch branch in cli-engine.ts around line 818 and is the single command exempted from the registry dispatchability assertion.
